Extending to approximately 205 sq.m / 2,207 sq.ft and standing on beautifully established grounds of approximately 0.32 hectares / 0.80 acres, Glenavon is a home of considerable charm and provenance, having been in the ownership of just two families since its construction between 1933 and 1935. The original owner, a native of Woodquay, drew inspiration from the classical architecture of Galway City Courthouse, incorporating its distinctive columns into the design of the residence. Many of the original architectural details associated with the 1930s remain evident today, including elegant geometric glazing to the front windows and entrance porch. Together with the striking courthouse-inspired columns, these features give Glenavon a unique and immediately recognisable architectural identity. Internally, the house is notable for its generous proportions and abundance of natural light. The ground-floor accommodation comprises an entrance hallway, a spacious family room with dual-aspect windows and feature fireplace, and a large formal dining room, also benefiting from dual-aspect windows and a feature fireplace. To the rear of the house is a cosy living room, a playroom with attractive bay window, kitchen with an oil stove, rear hallway and guest WC. The first-floor accommodation comprises the main family bathroom and four generously proportioned bedrooms. The large rear bedroom benefits from its own private WC, while two further bedrooms are of similar proportions. The particularly impressive principal bedroom is exceptionally spacious, enjoying dual-aspect windows. Throughout the house, the natural light, generous room proportions and surviving period details combine to retain the atmosphere and character of a bygone era while providing the space required for modern family living. The grounds are undoubtedly one of Glenavon's most appealing features. Thoughtfully laid out from the outset and developed over successive decades, the mature gardens contain a wonderful variety of features including meandering pathways, a wishing well, ornamental pond, internal and external stone garden walls and colourful established planting. The gardens provide an exceptional degree of privacy, colour and seasonal interest, while the orientation and layout allow the grounds to benefit from excellent sunlight from morning through to evening. Since acquiring Glenavon, the current owners have carefully extended and enhanced the residence while remaining sympathetic to its original character. The grounds have also been further developed, including the conversion of part of the former vegetable garden into a full-size lawn tennis court – a particularly rare recreational amenity within such a mature and private residential setting. The property enjoys an attractive rural setting while remaining exceptionally accessible to Galway City, Athenry and the principal employment centres on the eastern side of the city. For families, there is an excellent choice of primary and secondary schools within convenient reach. Cregmore National School is less than 1 km away, with Lackagh National School approximately 5 km from the property. Secondary-level schools are available in Claregalway, approximately 8 km away and Athenry, approximately 13 km away with school bus services available to both second level schools. Access to the M6 Motorway is approximately 11 km from the property, providing excellent connectivity towards Galway City, Athlone and the wider motorway network. Galway City Centre is approximately 18 km away, while Parkmore Business Park is approximately 12 km and the new Dexcom facility in Athenry approximately 13 km from the property. A home of enduring character and distinction, Glenavon represents a rare opportunity to acquire a substantial period residence where architectural heritage, mature private gardens and exceptional outdoor amenities combine to create a truly unique family home. Viewing is highly recommended to fully appreciate the character, proportions and setting of this wonderful property. No. 10 Newpark Lawn is an exceptionally attractive detached family residence, set within a mature and established residential enclave just off the Castlecomer Road in Kilkenny City. Beautifully presented both inside and out, the property combines generous, well-balanced accommodation with an impressive level of character, a wonderfully private rear garden and a highly convenient city location. The distinctive brick exterior, pitched gables and mature climbing greenery immediately give the house a strong sense of individuality. A carefully landscaped front garden, filled with established planting and colourful hydrangeas, creates excellent kerb appeal and provides a welcoming approach to the front entrance. A paved area surrounds the house, while gated side access leads conveniently through to the rear garden. Stepping inside, the entrance hall creates a memorable first impression. The combination of large-format tiled flooring, painted wall panelling and rich blue-green tones gives the space a confident and elegant finish. A feature staircase with a traditional runner forms an attractive focal point, while the generous hallway provides a natural and practical connection between the principal ground-floor rooms. The main living room is a bright, comfortable and generously proportioned family space. Timber flooring adds warmth, while the traditional fireplace provides a natural focal point. Wide glazed doors overlook the rear garden and allow natural light to fill the room, creating an excellent connection between the interior and the outdoor entertaining areas. The kitchen and dining space is designed as a sociable heart of the home, offering ample room for everyday family life and entertaining. The fitted kitchen provides generous storage and work surfaces with a feature Island, while the adjoining dining area opens directly onto the paved rear terrace. This arrangement allows the indoor and outdoor spaces to flow naturally together and is particularly well suited to summer dining and family gatherings. The first-floor accommodation is approached by an impressive split-level staircase, finished with a traditional tartan-style runner, painted wall panelling and rich blue tones. The high ceiling and open-tread section of the staircase add character and create a strong sense of light and space. From the central landing, there is access to five bedrooms and two separate bathroom facilities, providing an excellent arrangement. The roof structure is such that it holds mezzanine potential. The principal bedroom is a particularly generous and inviting room, measuring approximately 10'2" x 16'1". Its distinctive pitched ceiling and tall window create an attractive sense of height, while soft neutral finishes give the room a calm and comfortable atmosphere. An extensive bank of fitted wardrobes provides excellent built-in storage without compromising the proportions of the room. This room benefits from an en suite attractively presented with painted wall panelling, a pedestal wash-hand basin, WC, traditional-style radiator and complementary wood-effect flooring. Four further bedrooms are arranged around the landing. The second bedroom measures approximately 12'6" x 10'11" and is a bright, well-proportioned double room with a large window and ample space for freestanding furniture. The third bedroom, measuring approximately 11'0" x 12'9", also provides generous double accommodation and can comfortably incorporate a desk or dressing area, making it equally suitable as a bedroom, guest room or home office. A fourth double bedroom measures approximately 10'9" x 11'2" and benefits from good natural light and practical wall space for storage. The fifth bedroom measures approximately 8'2" x 11'3" and is presently arranged as a comfortable single room. A full wall of fitted wardrobes provides particularly useful storage, allowing the remaining floor area to be used efficiently. Taken together, the bedroom layout provides four comfortable double rooms and a generously sized single bedroom, offering considerable flexibility for family living, guests and working from home. The bedroom accommodation is served by two separate bathroom facilities. The larger main bathroom measures approximately 9'4" x 6'1" and is finished in a clean, contemporary style. It includes a spacious glazed walk-in shower, wash-hand basin and WC, with large-format wall tiling and wood-effect flooring creating a practical, low-maintenance finish. An additional bathroom or shower room, measuring approximately 9'2" x 3'2", provides valuable extra facilities for a busy household. The room is attractively presented with painted wall panelling, a pedestal wash-hand basin, WC, traditional-style radiator and complementary wood-effect flooring. The presence of two bathroom facilities on the bedroom level greatly enhances the practicality of this substantial five-bedroom family home. The rear garden is undoubtedly one of the property’s standout features. A broad paved terrace extends across the rear of the house, providing several areas for outdoor seating, dining and relaxation. Beyond the terrace is a central lawn surrounded by mature hedging, trees, flowering plants and thoughtfully arranged borders, creating a wonderful sense of privacy and enclosure. A timber pergola provides an additional sheltered seating area and adds further character to the garden. There is also a useful garden shed, raised planting, decorative lighting and ample space for children to play. The combination of established planting, sunny patio areas and a manageable lawn makes this an outdoor space that can be enjoyed throughout the year. Newpark Lawn is a mature residential setting offering excellent convenience to Kilkenny City Centre and the surrounding road network. Newpark Shopping Centre, MacDonagh Junction, local schools, medical facilities, Kilkenny Golf Club, recreational amenities and established public-transport links are all within easy reach. Access to the Kilkenny Ring Road and onward routes, including the M9 motorway, is also convenient. Ring Fran to view.
